tagline.text: An octagonal National Historical Landmark lighthouse guarding the Mactan Channel entrance in Liloan, Cebu

location.label: Location
location.text: Bagacay Point, Barangay Catarman, Liloan, Cebu (next to the Amara subdivision)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱100~500 (local transport and snacks from Cebu City; excludes flights and lodging)

children.text: Bagacay Point Lighthouse is an octagonal masonry lighthouse on a headland in Liloan, north of Cebu City, lighting the entrance to the Mactan Channel, and it is a National Historical Landmark. It is about a 30-45-minute drive from Cebu City, so it fits easily into a half-day trip.

Bagacay Point Lighthouse stands on a headland called Bagacay Point in Barangay Catarman, Liloan, on the northeast side of the island of Cebu. In the local Cebuano language a lighthouse is called a "parola," so it is also known as "Parola sa Liloan." Below it you can look out over the Mactan Channel between mainland Cebu and Mactan Island, and the light guides ships as they enter the northeast opening of the channel.
A light was first lit on this point in
under the Spanish colonial government. In
a cylindrical stone tower with a double balcony and lantern was built, and that older tower was switched off in
. The tower you see today dates from the American colonial period. Construction began under an executive order issued by William Howard Taft, then president of the Philippine Commission, on
, and the year
is carved above the tower door. Sources disagree on when it was first lit, giving either
April 1, 1905
or
. Remains of the older lighthouse are also said to survive beside the present tower.
The present tower is an octagonal structure of coral stone, concrete and masonry,
tall (about 72 feet). Some sources give
172 feet
, but the National Historical Commission (NHCP) marker says 72 feet, so the larger figure looks like an error. The light is a white flash every
5 seconds
(Fl W 5s), with a focal height of about
and a stated range of 20 nautical miles (about
37 km

). The NHCP marker says 17 nautical miles, so sources differ; think of it as roughly 17 to 20 nautical miles. It is still a working, solar-powered lighthouse operated by the Philippine Coast Guard's Cebu Station.
Bagacay Point Lighthouse was declared a National Historical Landmark by Resolution No. 7 of
, and the National Historical Institute (NHI), the predecessor of the NHCP, installed a marker in

. It is regarded as a notable example of American-era lighthouse architecture that survives in the Philippines. It is not a flashy attraction, though. You come for the white octagonal tower, the sea views and the feel of the small village below the point, which makes it a good short stop on a drive along Cebu's northern coast or a tour of Liloan town.
A white octagonal tower of coral stone and masonry stands on the headland. You can get close to the year
carved above the door and the lantern room above, which makes it popular with people who like architecture.
From the tip of the point the Mactan Channel and the sea toward Mactan Island open up widely. On clear days you can frame passing ships together with the distant outline of the island.
Remains of the Spanish-era lighthouse, first lit in
and replaced by a cylindrical stone tower in
, are said to survive beside the present tower. You can feel two layers of colonial history in one place.

blocks.title: Watching the light come on at dusk

children.text: After sunset you can watch a white flash every
5 seconds
. Because this is a working lighthouse run by the Coast Guard, the appeal is that the light really guides ships in the channel.

Whether you can climb the tower depends on the keeper and the Coast Guard. There is a record that the inner stairs were open in 2022, but the treads are rusted, so go slowly. Please check on the spot.
On the sea cliff below the lighthouse is a Spanish-era watchtower that locals call "Bantayan sa Hari." A blog review describes it as a few minutes' walk downhill from the lighthouse.
The Liloan town center (poblacion) has the San Fernando Rey parish church and the municipal hall, and Titay's, a rosquillos shop said to have been in business since
, is within walking distance. It pairs well with the lighthouse as a food stop.

items.title: Half-day trip from Cebu City
items.subtitle: Liloan town, the lighthouse and the coastal watchtower

children.text: Set out from Cebu City or Mactan. By car or Grab, expect about
30-45 minutes
from the city, heading north through Mandaue. Rush hour brings traffic, so leaving earlier is easier.
In the Liloan poblacion, first look around the San Fernando Rey parish church and the front of the municipal hall. Take in the feel of the town in front of the church and pick up something to drink.
Head toward Catarman and arrive at the lighthouse at the tip of the point. Walk around the tower and look at the year
above the door, the octagonal structure and the lantern room. Ask on the spot whether you can climb inside.
Walk down along the coast below the lighthouse toward the Bantayan sa Hari watchtower. The path can be slippery, so wear comfortable shoes and be careful at the cliff edge.
Return to the town center for lunch, buy rosquillos at Titay's, and head back to the city.

If you want to see the light come on, leave in the late afternoon, see the lighthouse around sunset, and keep a car waiting for the trip home. The point is dark at night, so avoid staying alone for long.

items.title: Northern coast combination
items.subtitle: Lagoon and Danao after the lighthouse

children.text: See the Liloan poblacion and the lighthouse first.
You can look around the Papa Kit's Marina fishing lagoon and the nearby beach area close to the lighthouse. Admission and prices change from time to time, so check on the spot.
Continue along the same national highway toward Danao City farther north. Boats to the Camotes Islands leave from Danao, so you can link it in if you have more days.
Flights run from Manila (NAIA) to Mactan–Cebu International Airport (CEB). Travel time and fares vary by airline and season, so check a booking site.
A blog says Liloan is only a few minutes by car from Mactan–Cebu International Airport. The exact travel time depends on traffic.

Take a Liloan-bound jeepney number 25 from near Sun Gold across from SM City Cebu or from the national highway in Mandaue, and get off near the 7-Eleven in front of San Fernando Rey parish church (per a 2017 blog; routes may change).

From there take a habal-habal (motorcycle taxi) or tricycle toward the point. According to a 2017 blog, the fare was ₱10 from the church to the bridge and ₱30 from the bridge to the lighthouse, and another 2017 blog gave ₱8-10 for a tricycle, but fares may have risen, so negotiate before you ride.
One blog describes paying a habal-habal driver ₱200 for a half-day ride that combined the lighthouse, Bantayan sa Hari and Papa Kit's, with waiting time included.
Search for "Bagacay Point Lighthouse" in a map app and follow the directions. The route goes north through Mandaue, Umapad and Tayud toward Catarman.
It is said to be next to the Amara subdivision, so ask locals if you have trouble finding it.
The dry season, December to May, is best for walking outdoors and for photos. On clear days the Mactan Channel and the opposite shoreline are sharp.
Early morning or dusk is best in the day. There is little shade on the point, so midday is very hot, and at dusk you can see the light come on.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: Most stable views and photos; peak visiting season
Strong midday sun, so go early in the morning or at dusk
On days of strong wind and waves stay away from the edge of the point and check the latest weather

Around the lighthouse is a residential and fishing-village area, so staying in Cebu City or Mactan and making a day trip is easier. The Liloan coast also has several small beach resorts, including around Pepito's Beach, if you want to relax for a day. Resort prices and rules differ, so check before you go.
Food centers on the Liloan poblacion. Titay's, a rosquillos shop said to have operated since

, is the best known, and near the municipal hall and the church some vendors sell "masi," sticky rice filled with mashed peanuts. Gaisano Grand Liloan, Jollibee and a food street are also close by, so meals are not a worry.
Enter the English name Bagacay Point Lighthouse in a map app, and on the spot ask for "Parola sa Liloan" or "the lighthouse next to Amara."
There is also a port town called Liloan at the southern tip of Cebu in Santander. Do not mix the two up; enter Liloan, Cebu together with the lighthouse name.
When using a habal-habal, agree on the fare and waiting time in advance. If you travel alone, a review says drivers wearing LIJODA (Liloan Joint Drivers Association) shirts are safer.
The point has little shade, so bring a hat, sunscreen and water. Midday sun is strong, so early morning or late afternoon is more comfortable.
The lighthouse is a government facility run by the Coast Guard. When photographing close to it, follow signs and staff instructions, and check locally whether drones are allowed.
Whether you can climb the tower and the entrance fee vary by source, so confirm locally. Even if you cannot climb, the point and the sea views are worth seeing on their own.
Combining Liloan church, Titay's rosquillos and Papa Kit's Marina fills a half day. If time is short, see only the lighthouse and the church.
There is a record that the tread of the inner stairs is rusted, and it is unclear whether the interior is open. Go slowly, and do not force it if access is blocked.
The edge of the point and the sea cliff below are slippery and windy. Be careful not to step backward while taking photos.
Entrance fees and whether the tower interior is open differ by source. Confirm with staff on the spot, and politely decline if an unofficial guide demands a fee.
There are reports that Typhoon Tino in November 2025 damaged parts of Liloan. No damage to the lighthouse was reported, but check local conditions first right after a typhoon.
There is little lighting around the point at night, so use a waiting vehicle after dark.
Habal-habal fares are not fixed, so agree on the destination, price and whether the driver waits before you ride.

It is in the same municipality as the lighthouse, and the poblacion with the San Fernando Rey parish church, the municipal hall and the rosquillos shops is within the same town, reached by car or habal-habal.
Continue north along the same national highway to reach Danao, where boats to the Camotes Islands depart.
Across the Mactan Channel seen from the lighthouse is Mactan Island. It has the airport and resort areas, so it is easy to combine.
An island group reached by boat from Danao, which you can plan together if you have more days.
The central city is about a
30-45-minute
drive from the lighthouse.
